ID verification= 101 ways to kill a game. Yeah. No thanks. I'd literally delete all my content and remove my account if that happened.
Age related safety systems require a way to verify the age of a user otherwise they would be easily abused and have no value or provide no solution. 
Tools already exist in the game to deal with this. Reporting with an actual moderation ticket and proof, as well as blocking a user. 
In order to set age related safety, all users would have to provide a government issued ID which can also be used. As kids could and would just use their parents ID. 
Age related safety is simply not possible without verification of age. 
This would directly impact all users while not providing a solution to the issue and would directly impact the viability of the platform. It doesn't seem like a viable solution at all. 
Education should be at the forefront of anyone's mind who wishes to prevent this form of issue. Using already existing tools and educating young teens so they are aware of the dangers of the world and virtually all internet platforms is important and may fall mostly on the shoulders of the peers of the young teen. 
As there is simply no way to have age related safety setting without verification of age, this canny is unviable. Not saying methods shouldn't be considered, I've listed some myself and the game already has viable tools, but this canny as written isn't viable.
@{5f99a97e4d4afb3fb6674ca5|full_name}: I did not mention ID verification, how did you manage to assume that from my post?

@{5f99a97e4d4afb3fb6674ca5|full_name}: Facebook, Steam already requires DoB (Date of Birth) to be entered to create an account, this would be hilariously easy to implement. You'd be better off acknowledging that kids who are truthful when creating an account would be much better off not seeing content and interacting with people which violate section 12d of the VRChat TOS.
All you have to do is link a Steam account or make an Oculus account and content filters would be put in place in the background, avatars marked as obscene or that contain gore could simply show up as errors for these users.
Quest accounts could simply be restricted from seeing all obscene-labelled content given the age-distribution of their user-base.
VRChat already has it so visitors who enter through the tutorial meet up with other visitors after they go through one of the portals, it would be easy to just make it to where they pair-up in instances with the most visitors and new trust ranks for a few hours.

Hi, I'm Furriest. I am federally underage, and have been on the platform for a long time now 2-3+ years, and throughout that time I have been subject to lots of harassment, and inappropriate behaviors and interactions from adult figures that, due to the anonymity of VRChat by nature, cannot be moderated/policed effectively due to the fact that VRChat's moderation system does not handle private instances very well among small groups of individuals, and that VRChat is still in development. 
Hosted among communities of these people were a very rare dozen malicious individuals who corrupted my views of sexuality among other things when I just-entered the platform. Due to the nature of these encounters on this platform, I have had a-lot more struggles on the emotional and academic environment because being taken advantage of is really painful.
For these reasons, I ask that there be effective algorithms in-place that better separate age-groups to prevent the behaviors I've been subjected to, manipulated into thinking for a time to be acceptable, and have experienced from older-aged users. Hopefully, this system is able to prevent the cultural environments that cause these issues, and is secure or  hard to bypass by users, comparable to the trust system.
In summary, VRChat should be able to detect users who use and create inappropriate avatars via a moderation system that can properly flag NSFW avatars that are not labeled as NSFW via the "report avatar as inappropriate" feature, and algorithmically blacklist a good-majority of users from seeing them, along with ensuring that VRChat does its best to keep instances separated by its age-groups for these flagged users.
If a system cannot be made to attempt separate individuals by age group (when an instance is being made and when players join public instances), a better system would be to have an automatically enabled setting that disables all inappropriate avatars from being seen by these users (mostly quest users), along with harsher moderation for the creators who did not label these avatars as such.
title: [Platform Safety] Algorithm/System to better separate individuals by age group & trust rank; prevent inappropriate content/individuals from being seen by Quest accounts.
